Whole-entry overlay: an entry here REPLACES the auto-extracted entry for
the same canonical vtes.json name (compile stamps src:'hand'). Keys must
be canonical names — for vampires that includes the group suffix, e.g.
'Zip (G3)'. Entries follow the same shape as auto entries (see
elysium-cardfx-design.md) and MAY carry richer keys (bloodToPool,
handSize, trifle, unique, costEdge, note, ...) — consumers ignore keys
they don't know. Every entry below is verified against the printed
card_text in vtes.json, not written from memory.
Curation queue policy: (1) all cards in shipped bot playbooks,
(2) TWDA-frequent staples, (3) anything the auto tier provably mistags.

Blood Doll.note: Master: put on your vampire; during their master phase move 1 blood vampire→pool OR pool→vampire (printed, verified in vtes.json 11 Sep 2026). TWO modes since track C (11 Sep): bloodToPool (consumed by _applyPhaseIncome, with the v0.6.104 last-blood floor) and poolToBlood (the reverse; consumer = the B2 income-direction decide — until then ignored per the unknown-key rule). `persistent` added 14 July (v1.4.0 follow-up): auto-tier would have given this via "put this card on" — added by hand since curated overlay replaces whole entries and never inherits new auto tags.

Vessel.note: Trifle. Put on a vampire (and you may burn a Blood Doll — unmodelled); during their UNLOCK phase move 1 blood vampire→pool OR pool→vampire (printed, verified in vtes.json 11 Sep 2026). Two modes since track C, same split as Blood Doll; `phase`:'unlock' is a full phase later than Blood Doll's 'master' — the whole reason phase is per-mode data. `persistent` added 14 July (v1.4.0 follow-up).

modes.note: Inside-Dirt-100%-continued (19 July): the card states no phase restriction for this choice either, same as the blood-add mode -- phase:master is this bot implementation checking it at the same sensible point, not a rules requirement. Now WIRED: draws up to base(7)+2 immediately (the rulebook itself: 'immediately discard down to or draw up to your hand size' whenever it changes), tracked via _handSizeBonus and reverted (discard back to 7) at end of turn when the until-end-of-turn bonus expires.

the card ITSELF states no phase restriction ("You can lock this card to add 1 blood...", any time) -- phase:master here is this BOT implementation checking it once per turn at a sensible point, not a rules requirement, matching Arcane Library-class lock-income timing conventions this session already established

Dreams of the Sphinx.note: Inside-Dirt-100%-GO (19 July), continuing Life in the City: THREE bundled lock-choices the auto tier collapsed into one mode -- split into three separate modes so 'phase' (already a per-mode field elsewhere) and a new mode-level costEdge can each carry their own precondition. New _considerLockIncome(phaseKey) consumer, called at unlock (pool-gain) and master (blood-add) phases -- same shape as the existing _considerTurnActGrants (scan unlocked board permanents, decide(), lock+apply), generalized for income instead of actGrant so Arcane Library/Chantry (both lock-based income masters) can reuse the same reader later.

Inside Dirt.note: Ⓓ Burn the Edge to burn 3 blood from another Methuselah's vampire OR 3 pool from your prey. Pool damage that is not a bleed — the canonical 'block this even though it isn't a bleed' example. No `persistent`: a one-shot Action, no location/put-in-play text — confirmed correctly excluded by the v1.4.0 sweep.

The Parthenon.note: Unique location. During your master phase, you can lock this card to get +1 master phase action. No host vampire — a Location doesn't attach to one. The text does NOT say "as a master phase action", so locking costs no existing action slot: pure profit whenever the card is in play, unlocked, and not yet used this turn. `actGrant` is ENTRY-LEVEL here (verified against `_recomputePhaseActs`'s actual read — `h.e.actGrant`, not per-mode — the design doc's "per-mode" wording was aspirational and never actually implemented that way; fixed in cardfx-design.md 14 July). Read by the new `_considerTurnActGrants(phaseKey)` (bot v0.5+, 14 July): the lock decision (`decide('lock-actgrant')`) is currently UNCONDITIONAL for this card since it has no real tradeoff — a future multi-choice `persist:'turn'` card (Dreams-of-the-Sphinx-style) will need its own weighed branch there, not a change to the reader itself.

Information Highway.note: Unique location. +2 transfers — a permanent influence-phase action baseline increase for as long as this stays in play. Read by the EXISTING `_recomputePhaseActs()` (built and unit-tested 14 July against a synthetic card; this is the first REAL card to exercise it). No lock, no choice — pure Passive.

Ashur Tablets.note: Put this card in play. Only one Ashur Tablets can be played each turn. If YOU control three copies of this card, remove all copies in play (even controlled by other Methuselahs) from the game to gain 3 pool and choose up to 13 ash-heap cards (1 to hand, shuffle the rest into your library). A THRESHOLD/one-shot-per-trigger mechanic, not recurring income — deliberately given NO `modes`/`phase`/`actGrant` (the auto tier's old `poolGain:3` was a mistag; see `cardfx-persistent-lock-design-decisions.md` §8 for why this doesn't generalize to a schema tag). `handler` (v1.4.2, 14 July): the OWN-side mechanism is now automated via CARD_HANDLERS['ashur-tablets'], dispatched after every play, checking the bot's own copies in `ready`. Removal targets the client's `'burned'` zone (removed-from-the-game, distinct from `'ash'`), a local board mutation exactly like `_toAsh`'s pattern, just a different destination. The 12-copy shuffle-back uses the EXISTING `pileBulk{lib,shuffle}` wire verb (untested by the bot before this card — unlike `drawCrypt`, no prior in-bot usage to lean on). The 1-to-hand pick is scored (`_ashScoreFor`): Master bonus + decklist-scarcity (qty minus everywhere the bot can currently see a copy) + hand-type-mix — a GENERAL v1 foundation, explicitly not persona-weighted yet (Johan's call: theorize/playtest toward tuning later, see the design-decisions doc §11). Deliberately OUT of scope, unbuilt: removing OTHER Methuselahs' copies — `ctrl` is owner-gated, no existing mechanism reaches across the table; the bot's OWN 3 copies are removed regardless, matching the rule as far as it can reach.

Leverage.note: Verified card_text (16 July, vtes.json upload): 'Only usable during a bleed action. Burn the Edge to get +1 bleed that does not count against the limit. You cannot gain the Edge this action. If you would get the Edge, it is burned instead.' No discipline requirement, no blood/pool cost beyond the Edge itself. `costEdge` (steg 2, 15 July): the auto tier already produced fx.bleed:1 correctly but has no way to extract an Edge REQUIREMENT from prose, so this whole entry moves to the hand tier for that field -- Inside Dirt carries the same flag but nothing else consumes it yet; read by `_bestBleedModifierFor`/`_playBleedModifier`. `edgeLock` (steg 4, 16 July): the 'cannot gain the Edge this action' clause -- steg 2 wrongly assumed a burned-then-regranted Edge was two unrelated rulebook events; the REAL text says the opposite, caught only once the actual card_text was available. Also per the official ruling [LSJ 20100218]/[RTR 20180511-2] quoted on this card: 'A limited bleed modifier can be played before or after' the block decision -- Leverage itself is NOT limited (explicitly exempt: 'does not count against the limit'), but this confirms Conditioning/Bonding's own (limited) modifiers share Leverage's identical 'during a bleed action' timing rather than being pre-block-exclusive.

Seduction.note: Verified card_text (16 July, vtes.json upload): 'Only usable as the action is announced. [dom] Choose a younger vampire. The chosen vampire cannot block this action. [DOM] As above, but choose any vampire.' Genuinely different from Conditioning/Bonding/Leverage: a BLOCK-PREVENTION effect (targets a specific opposing vampire, not a bleed-amount change), strictly pre-announce-only (no 'before or after' flexibility), and the [dom] mode needs GENERATION comparison ('younger') which no current bot code tracks at all. Official ruling on file: must be played (along with any other 'as the action is announced' modifier) BEFORE modifiers that aren't restricted to that moment (e.g. Conditioning) -- a real sequencing constraint once a pre-block window exists. Deliberately NOT built this session (16 July) -- `t`/`req` reproduced here verbatim from the (otherwise-correct) auto tier purely so this curated override doesn't blank them out (curated is a whole-entry replacement -- see cardfx-compile.js), no fx/modes assigned yet. Needs, in order: (1) the pre-block "when announced" window itself (design-decisions.md §13 step 2), (2) generation data surfaced somewhere the bot can read it, (3) a new fx concept (e.g. fx.preventBlock naming a target) plus the wire/log convention to tell a defending bot which of ITS OWN vampires is disqualified from _pickBlocker's candidates, (4) the Seduction-before-Conditioning sequencing rule once both can coexist in the same window. Flagged as its own follow-up phase, not invented ahead of that design work.

Effective Management.note: Master. Move the top card from your crypt to your uncontrolled region. One-shot: no location/put-in-play text, confirmed NOT persistent by the v1.4.0 sweep — deliberately carries no `persistent` field here either, matching auto. The bot's master-play loop (v0.5+, 14 July) branches on `persistent` and ashes a card like this one instead of leaving it on the board forever — this card was the concrete motivating case for that fix. `handler` (v1.4.1, 14 July): the effect ITSELF is now automated too — CARD_HANDLERS['effective-management'] sends the EXISTING `drawCrypt` wire verb (the same one the bot's own paid Influence-phase vampire fetch already uses), just without paying the 4 transfers + 1 pool. No new crypt-tracking needed; 'top of crypt' isn't a player choice at all (a shuffled stack position, not a decision), so this needed no decide() — just a guard on `cryptN > 0`. No more human ctrl-correction needed for this card.

Marked Path.note: fas C (16 July): the two-step mechanic is BUILT. Step 1 (attach): only after a SUCCESSFUL directed action -- put on the acting vampire, recording the action's target Methuselah and the mode's stealth value. Step 2 (burn): during a LATER action by THIS vampire against the SAME target, burn for +1/+2 stealth (_bestStealthFor offers board-attached copies whose recorded target matches). fx.stealthLater deliberately NOT fx.stealth: the generic hand-scan stealth finders must never misplay it as instant stealth -- the fas-A misplay guard, now structural. v1.5.0 (17 July): persistent:true added -- the curated tier REPLACES auto wholesale, and this entry had silently dropped the flag the auto tier derives from 'put this card on' (found by the fas B/C sweep's curated-drift check).

Elder Impersonation.note: fas C (16 July): the superior mode is BUILT -- fx.cancelBlock: played when a minion attempts to block; that attempt fails outright and that minion cannot attempt again (the defender's attempted-set, registered at attempt time since fas A+, makes the exclusion automatic on receipt of the frozen cancel line). Basic +1 stealth unchanged. Card text verified fas A.

Perfectionist.note: fas C (16 July): BUILT. archetype:true -- attaches to a vampire at master play (one archetype per vampire, the attach gate enforces it). fx.bloodAfterCleanAction: once each turn, +1 blood after a successful action during which no reaction cards were played -- the bot's actor-side hook fires on a clean through (conservative v1 read: 'clean' = the ask was never contested and no bounce moved the target; a reaction card played without contesting would be missed, documented). Blood capped at capacity per the rulebook.

Wider View.note: Inside-Dirt-100%-GO (19 July), the last card. Source-verified vekn.net first: normal crypt draw costs 4 transfers + 1 pool (already the bots own baseline, elysium-bot.js influence-phase loop); Wider Views 1-transfer swap is dramatically cheaper but FORCES removing an existing uncontrolled crypt card from the game -- Johans own described use case (swap a duplicate you already have). NEITHER ability is lock-gated (unlike Dreams of the Sphinx) -- both are plain transfer-spending options, repeatable while transfers remain. New transferSwap/transferBurnPool fx keys + a shared transferCost (both need it, but for different amounts) -- a new consumer class the bot genuinely lacked until now, wired directly into the EXISTING influence-phase loop rather than a new decide() window, since transfers are already tracked there as this.inf.

Shadow Cast.note: v1.5.0 (17 July, fas B/C sweep): Marked Path's true twin -- same attach window ('Only usable after resolution of a successful directed action'), same same-target binding ('directed at the same Methuselah or same set'), burn = +1. [obl] is ORDINARY instant stealth (hand-playable via _bestStealthFor); only [OBL] attaches, and the attach flow's per-mode stealthLater scan + _modeUsableBy keeps basic-obl vampires out of it. The other three template siblings (Zip Line, Pass Through Shadow, Under My Skin) attach through their OWN play (action/combat/modifier), NOT the post-success window -- they get stealthLater WITHOUT attachAfterSuccess from the compiler and stay safely inert for the bot.

Forced Confessional.note: v1.5.0 (17 July, fas B/C sweep): Elder Impersonation's exact template in DOMINATE -- header 'Only usable if a minion attempts to block', [DOM] 'That attempt fails and the blocking minion cannot attempt to block this action again', zero extra conditions/costs/side-effects (the per-card condition audit that kept 13 template-mates OUT: age comparisons, blocker-type gates, 'other than the acting minion', lock/combat riders -- none of which _bestCancelBlockFor checks). [dom] basic is -1 blocker intercept: no auto vocabulary key, deliberately left unencoded rather than guessed. First cancelBlock for the default Dominate weenie archetype.

Relentlessness.note: v1.5.0 (17 July, fas B/C sweep): the second EI-exact template hit ('Only usable if a minion attempts to block. That attempt fails and...' verbatim, no extra conditions). OR-headers ('[cel] or [for]' / '[CEL] or [FOR]') follow the v1.5.0 convention: one mode per alternative, so _modeUsableBy keeps its single-requirement view. Costs 1 blood (printed cost, entry-level -- _bestCancelBlockFor checks it against the acting vampire).

Enticement.note: v1.5.0 (17 July, fas B/C sweep): DELIBERATELY INERT curation -- a live-misplay guard, not a playbook. The auto tier gave this [ser D] poolDmg:2 / [SER D] poolDmg:3 with no costEdge: _bestPoolDmgActionFor would have played it WITHOUT the Edge (it is the cost: 'Burn the Edge to burn 2 pool from your prey') and, worse, ignored the rider 'Minions you control cannot bleed until the end of the turn' -- a self-restriction the engine cannot yet represent, so the bot would bleed right after in the same turn: a rules violation. costEdge:true (v1.5.0 auto also derives it now) + EMPTY mode fx = the card is never picked. Re-arm poolDmg here only when a bleed-lockout mechanism exists (backlog).

Stunt Cycle.note: Restlist aftermath (18 July): the auto tier double-failed here -- a PHANTOM [cel] mode born from the mid-text bracket in "If the OPPOSING minion has Celerity [cel] ..." (an opponent clause, tagged as ours, prevent:all on a scanned combat key), and the [POT] text "4R damage" missed the strike pattern so it inherited strike:3. Soak.note: Grinder onboarding (18 July): the Wall of Filth pattern -- "Prevent 2 NON-aggravated damage" breaks the prevent regex on the middle word AND ghost-tags aggr via the direction-blind /aggravated/ match. Curated to the printed values; the non-aggravated restriction is unmodeled (auto-tolerant: the value is right in the common case, marginally generous against aggravated strikes).

Hidden Strength.note: 20 Sep 2026 (Johan): printed 'Prevent X+1 damage' with X = blood paid. fx.prevent 1 stays the FREE floor (X = 0) and fx.preventX marks that the player may pay X blood for X more -- the bot pays what the incoming hit needs (Johan: no real downside to preventing it ALL: mostly used against aggravated damage, and it denies Pulled Fangs-class effects that need the opposing vampire to deal more damage than mine). [FOR] adds the optional press. Was (18 July): the conservative floor only.

Call the Lamprey.note: Combat GO (steal-blood family, 19 July): the auto tier gave [obt] and [OBT] the SAME stealBlood:1 -- but only [OBT] (superior) reads "steal 1 blood from the opposing minion" (unrestricted); [obt] (inferior) is "steal 1 blood from the opposing ally. Only usable during combat with an ally" -- a target-type restriction (ally vs vampire) the bot cannot verify (no ally-vs-vampire combat distinction modeled). [obt] emptied to prevent a misplay against a vampire opponent; [OBT] kept clean.

The Khabar: Honor.note: Combat GO (strike-bonus family, 19 July): the auto tier tagged strike:3, but the card is "Only usable if this Assamite has been chosen for a contract on the opposing minion" -- a per-vampire contract-state precondition the bot cannot verify (2-card class total with Open Dossier; too small for a general req flag). Emptied to prevent an unverifiable-precondition misplay, same discipline as req.title/req.rangeClose.

Taste of Vitae.note: Combat GO, Taste of Vitae (19 July): unique in the whole database -- the only card with "gains blood equal to the amount lost by the opposing vampire to damage this round". CORRECTED 25 July (the Nosferatu inventory caught it): the card is DISCIPLINE-FREE -- the 19 July curation's abo gates were a data bug (full text verified: no [abo] anywhere; disciplines: undefined). Dormant until now (no tracked deck carried it); single at:null mode restores reachability.

Life in the City.note: Inside-Dirt-100%-GO (19 July): auto tier already gave bloodAdd:1+bloodAddTo:own-ready correctly (v1.6.3 pattern) -- curated purely to ADD the handler key (own-ready target-selection + application is a genuine choice needing code, like Effective Management, not an automatic phase-income trigger the existing _applyPhaseIncome host-scan can reach, since this card has no host and resolves once, not persistently).

modes.note: the +1 transfer ability -- out of scope for the hand-size sweep (19 July); no transfer-mechanic consumer exists yet, left deliberately untagged rather than guessed at

Ennoia's Theater.note: Hand-size sweep continued (19 July): auto tier correctly detects handSize:1 as the shape needing curation (lock/phase have never been auto-settable by this compiler -- checked directly, no mode.phase= assignment exists anywhere in cardfx-compile.js). Curated mode 1 mirrors Dreams of the Sphinxs own handSize mode EXACTLY (lock:true, phase:master, fx:{handSize:1}) so _considerLockIncome needs zero new code for this second card -- proving the reader really is reusable, not just built for one card.

Chantry.note: The last card on phase-income-v2-plan.md (19 July). Source-verified vekn.net first: burn 1 pool OR 1 blood from a ready Tremere you control (flexible cost -- the official ruling confirms Rescue-from-Torpor is a standardized action type where cost splits between the payer and the rescued vampire, though Chantry itself only offers the two pure options, not a split). Measured the whole family first: only 3 cards mention torpor+ready-region at all, and the other two (Renewed Vigor -- host-attached, unlock-phase, burn-itself; Torpid Blood -- a global Gehenna-era event) share NOTHING structurally with Chantrys lock-based shape, so rescueTorpor is Chantry-specific vocabulary, not a guessed-at generalization. req.clan (already auto-detected) supplies WHICH clan both the torpor-target and the ready-payer must be -- reused, not duplicated into a new field. v1 scope: only rescues the BOTS OWN torpored Tremere (the card text technically allows helping ANY players Tremere, per official ruling their controller -- multiplayer-diplomacy-style altruism is out of scope, no infrastructure for it).

Arcane Library.note: The cheapest-win pick (19 July), predicted back at Dreams of the Sphinxs own delivery -- _considerLockIncome already reads this exact shape (lock+phase+bloodAdd+bloodAddTo:unc), so only phase/bloodAddTo needed curating (auto tier already had req.clan+bloodAdd:1 right). The ONE new wrinkle: unlike Dreams of the Sphinxs own bloodAdd (any uncontrolled vampire), this card requires the TARGET to also be the matching clan (Tremere) -- _considerLockIncome needed a clan-aware target filter added, since its existing scan had no clan check at all (Dreams of the Sphinx never needed one).
